questions.prompt: What is the difference between distraction and interruption?
questions.answer: Distraction may divert attention; interruption suspends the ongoing task.

questions.prompt: Why might an unfinished task affect a new one?
questions.answer: Some attention can remain engaged with the prior task.
questions.feedback: Do not infer a universal duration or effect.

questions.prompt: What makes a resumption cue useful?
questions.answer: It specifies the prior state and next verifiable action.
questions.feedback: Write a cue, not just a task name.

questions.prompt: When should a protected session be interrupted?
questions.answer: When safety or a legitimate time-critical duty requires it.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only. Use answer-specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Classifies interruptions proportionately, preserves urgent obligations and demonstrates reliable resumption.
scoring.transfer: Design a five-entry simulated interruption log for a different work or learning context. Distinguish source, urgency, response and resumption cost; propose one team-level change and one individual change. Explain what would make either inappropriate.
scoring.pass: All four mapped course criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety boundaries. Quiz score alone cannot certify competency.
